I1.quote: A Micromeritics ASAP 2020 HD analyzer was used for surface area using nitrogen gas and low pressure hydrogen measurements. The sorption measurements were obtained using ultra-high purity grade (99.999%) gases at 77 K.

I2.quote: Searched for H2 uptake measured on a majority-carbon sorbent (e.g. rGO or GO alone). Not found: Fig. 7 and the text give H2 uptake only for Zr-MOF and the rGO/Zr-MOF composite (about 1% rGO).

I3.quote: There was also an enhancement of the hydrogen storage capacity of the rGO/Zr-MOF composite (1.8 wt% when compared with that of pristine Zr-MOF (1.4 wt%)) (Fig. 7). Since hydrogen measurements were conducted at only 1 bar
I3.location: main, p. 5 (journal p. 454), Section 3 Results and discussion; Fig. 7 (x axis 'Absolute pressure (mbar)', 0-1000); 77 K from Section 2.4

I4.quote: The rGO/Zr-MOF composite had a surface area of 1480 m2/g, whereas that of pristine Zr-MOF was 1116 m2/g.
I4.location: main, p. 4 (journal p. 453), Section 3 Results and discussion (Fig. 6, N2 sorption)

I5.quote: A composite material consisting of Zr-based metal organic framework (Zr-MOF) and reduced graphene oxide (rGO) was successfully synthesized by an in situ method.

notes: The only H2 sorbents measured are pristine Zr-MOF and the in situ rGO/Zr-MOF composite (Fig. 7 caption: 'Hydrogen sorption isotherms of Zr-MOF and rGO/Zr-MOF composite'; only these two curves are plotted). The composite is majority MOF by mass: synthesis used ZrCl4 (2.34 g), H2BDC (1.66 g) and 0.04 g of rGO (main, p. 2, Section 2.3), and the text refers to 'the relatively low quantity of rGO (1%) used in the preparation the composite material' (main, p. 4, Section 3). MOFs are not carbon sorbents under protocol §3, and a composite counts only if carbon is the majority component by mass. GO and rGO were characterized (PXRD, SEM, TEM) but no H2 uptake was measured on them. I3 and I4 were assessed for completeness and are met (77 K, up to ~1 bar; N2 surface areas, method not named, for both measured samples).
